APPROVE — as a bounded experiment, not proof that RunPod guarantees online attached resize.

Hold STOP through shader warmup/`MEASURING`. At the quiescent checkpoint, record `dvrlt6yk2k`’s API size/datacenter, mount/device and visible capacity, pod/PID with continuing ticks, and control hashes. Keep all network writers quiescent through verification. Submit only the console size change 200→500; cancel before confirmation on any restart, detach, format, or data-loss warning.

After Update, verify returned ID/size/datacenter, unchanged volume/mount/pod identity, continuing ticks, exact hashes, and no observable I/O errors. Run one create→write→`fsync`→read/compare→unlink test in a new diagnostic directory. Record visible capacity without remounting or restarting to force it. API success plus this small test does not prove all 500 units are usable or establish general online-resize support.

A failed, timed-out, or otherwise ambiguous update—or any identity/mount change, hash mismatch, or I/O error—ends the attempt: preserve state/logs, with no retry, remount, restart, deletion, or formatting. Resume writers only after acceptance. Approval assumes the retained persistent backup is the owner-accepted recovery point.
